User & customer journey

Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it.

  1. 01Discover & evaluate1 automation
  2. 02Sign up & activate2 automations
  3. 03Convert & pay1 automation
  4. 04Use, match & get help4 automations
  5. 05Renew & retain3 automations

01

Discover & evaluate

Prospects compare options, read docs and pricing, start a trial or request a demo. For B2B and AI products, usage during the trial is the clearest sign of who is serious and who needs help.

Touchpoints

  • Website and pricing page
  • Docs and API reference
  • Demo request form
  • Free trial or free plan
  • App store listing

Accountable owner

Growth or revenue operations lead

Automations on this stage

Discover & evaluate · 3–5 weeks

Product-qualified lead and demo routing

Demo requests and trial accounts that cross agreed usage and fit thresholds reach the right account executive with a usage brief and a booking link, while low-fit signups stay in self-serve journeys.

View the blueprint ↗
02

Sign up & activate

New users and new supply partners reach a first meaningful outcome: a workspace with real data, a first listing approved, a first useful AI result. Most churn starts here, so activation gets its own definition and owner.

Touchpoints

  • Signup and consent notice
  • Onboarding checklist
  • Welcome email and push
  • Seller or provider application
  • Verification queue

Accountable owner

Product or growth lead; marketplace operations lead for supply

Automations on this stage

Sign up & activate · 3–4 weeks

Event-driven onboarding and activation journeys

In-product tips, email, push and opt-in WhatsApp messages triggered by what each new user or workspace has and has not done, stopping the moment the activation milestone is reached.

View the blueprint ↗Sign up & activate · 5–7 weeks

Supply-side onboarding and verification queue

Seller, provider or host applications are collected in one structured flow, checked automatically where a reliable source exists, and decided by a reviewer working from a checklist in a single queue.

View the blueprint ↗
03

Convert & pay

Trials end, plans are chosen and payment mandates are set up. Notices must be clear about price, renewal date and how to cancel, and Indian card and UPI mandates need one-time authentication at registration.

Touchpoints

  • Trial ending notices
  • Plan and pricing page
  • Checkout and mandate setup
  • GST invoice
  • Sales-assisted proposal

Accountable owner

Revenue or monetization lead

Automations on this stage

Convert & pay · 2–4 weeks

Trial-to-paid nudges with clear renewal notices

Trial reminders tailored to what each account actually used, stating the conversion date, the price including any GST and the cancellation route plainly, with high-fit trials flagged to sales.

View the blueprint ↗
04

Use, match & get help

Customers use the product day to day, marketplace users find matches and anyone stuck asks for help. Support, matching, moderation and AI review queues decide whether the experience feels dependable.

Touchpoints

  • In-app chat and help center
  • Support tickets
  • Match and saved-search alerts
  • Listings, reviews and messages
  • AI output feedback

Accountable owner

Support, trust and safety, or operations lead

Automations on this stage

Use, match & get help · 4–6 weeks

Docs-grounded support assistant with human handoff

An assistant that answers how-to questions only from your current docs and changelog, cites its sources, says it is an AI, and hands billing, account, security and uncertain cases to a person with a summary.

View the blueprint ↗Use, match & get help · 3–5 weeks

Two-sided matching alerts

New demand is matched against providers' saved criteria and availability, the best-fit providers are notified on the channel they chose, and operations steps in when a request stays unfilled.

View the blueprint ↗Use, match & get help · 5–8 weeks

Trust and safety moderation queue

Listings, reviews, profiles and messages are screened with rules and a moderation model, risky items are held for trained moderators, and every decision, notice and appeal is recorded with a policy reason.

View the blueprint ↗Use, match & get help · 4–6 weeks

Human review queue for low-confidence AI outputs

Outputs that fail validators, fall below a confidence threshold or touch sensitive categories are held and routed to qualified reviewers, and their corrections feed the evaluation set.

View the blueprint ↗
05

Renew & retain

Renewals, failed payments, usage drops and public reviews decide whether revenue stays. Signals should reach a person early enough to help, and payment recovery should never read like a threat.

Touchpoints

  • Renewal and pre-debit notices
  • Failed-payment messages
  • Account health reviews
  • App Store and Google Play reviews
  • Cancellation flow

Accountable owner

Customer success or lifecycle lead

Automations on this stage

Renew & retain · 3–4 weeks

Failed-payment recovery and mandate-aware dunning

Payment failures are classified by cause and channel: India-issued card and UPI renewals get a link to authenticate or switch payment method, store subscriptions follow App Store and Google Play rules, and key accounts reach a person before any downgrade.

View the blueprint ↗Renew & retain · 4–6 weeks

Churn-risk alerts from usage drops

A weekly account health model spots falling usage, seat drops, departed champions and support spikes ahead of renewal, and gives the customer success owner an evidence-linked brief and a task.

View the blueprint ↗Renew & retain · 2–3 weeks

App store review response drafting

New App Store and Google Play reviews are collected, classified and answered with drafts that follow each store's reply policies and are approved by a person, with bug and billing reports turned into tickets.

View the blueprint ↗
06

Learn, ship & report

Feedback becomes roadmap decisions, releases are explained to the people who asked for them, AI quality is measured before and after each change, and investors receive numbers that reconcile with the books.

Touchpoints

  • NPS and in-app surveys
  • Roadmap and issue tracker
  • Release notes and changelog
  • Evaluation dashboards
  • Monthly investor update

Accountable owner

Founder with product, engineering and finance leads

Automations on this stage

Learn, ship & report · 3–5 weeks

Feedback-to-roadmap loop with release notes

Survey answers, reviews, tickets and sales notes are tagged into one feedback base linked to Jira, and when a fix or feature ships, release notes are drafted and sent to the users who asked for it.

View the blueprint ↗Learn, ship & report · 4–6 weeks

AI evaluation pipeline and cost-per-task monitoring

A versioned evaluation set runs on every prompt, model or retrieval change before release, production samples are scored on the same rubric, and cost per validated task is tracked by feature, customer and model route.

View the blueprint ↗Learn, ship & report · 3–5 weeks

Monthly investor and board metrics update

Revenue, pipeline, product and cost data are calculated with agreed definitions after month-end close, reconciled against the books, and drafted into an update the founder edits and sends.

View the blueprint ↗

Where people stay in control

Human checkpoints across the journey.

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
Product-qualified lead and demo routingDiscover & evaluateThe account executive reads the brief and decides whether, when and how to reach out. Revenue operations approves scoring rules and routing changes, and no sales email is sent automatically.
Event-driven onboarding and activation journeysSign up & activateThe product or growth lead approves every message, cap and stop rule before launch and reviews the weekly cohort view. Changes to the activation definition need product and revenue sign-off.
Supply-side onboarding and verification queueSign up & activateA trained operations reviewer approves, rejects or requests more information for every application. The model never rejects anyone, and high-risk categories and appeals go to a senior reviewer.
Trial-to-paid nudges with clear renewal noticesConvert & payThe revenue lead approves pricing copy, extension rules and any discount beyond the agreed band. Your legal or compliance owner reviews any trial that collects a card or mandate upfront, since India's guidelines treat forcing payment details for a free subscription as a subscription trap.
Two-sided matching alertsUse, match & get helpOperations staff handle unfilled and high-value requests personally. The marketplace lead reviews ranking rules for fairness and approves any change to how providers are ordered.
Trust and safety moderation queueUse, match & get helpTrained moderators decide removals and warnings; suspensions and bans need a senior reviewer. Law enforcement requests and legal notices go to the grievance officer and counsel, never to automation.
Docs-grounded support assistant with human handoffUse, match & get helpSupport agents own every refund, account change, security report and data request. The support lead approves which sources the assistant may use and reviews the weekly sample before its scope expands.
Human review queue for low-confidence AI outputsUse, match & get helpQualified reviewers, such as domain experts for legal, financial or health-adjacent outputs, approve or correct each held item before release. The product owner sets thresholds and sensitive categories.
Failed-payment recovery and mandate-aware dunningRenew & retainFinance owns the grace-period and downgrade policy. Customer success decides manual extensions or invoice payment for key accounts, and this workflow never deletes account data.
Churn-risk alerts from usage dropsRenew & retainThe customer success manager decides whether to call, run a training session, involve product or propose commercial terms. Discounts and contract changes need revenue lead approval.
App store review response draftingRenew & retainThe community or support lead approves or edits every reply before it is posted. Refunds for store purchases follow App Store and Google Play processes and are never promised in a reply.
Feedback-to-roadmap loop with release notesLearn, ship & reportProduct managers decide priorities and confirm every suggested merge. The product owner approves release notes, and the engineering lead reviews notes on security fixes and breaking changes before publication.
AI evaluation pipeline and cost-per-task monitoringLearn, ship & reportDomain reviewers label disputed samples and own the rubric. The product owner sets thresholds and decides whether a release that regresses on one measure may ship.
Monthly investor and board metrics updateLearn, ship & reportThe founder and finance lead sign off every number and every sentence before anything leaves the company. The workflow never emails investors directly.
